# NativeLink

> A high-performance remote build cache and remote execution platform for build
> systems that speak the Remote Execution API — Bazel, Buck2, Siso, Pants, Goma,
> and CMake via recc. Open source, written in Rust.

These docs are ordered as a ladder, not a catalogue. Each rung assumes the one
below it is standing, and each page states the rung it sits on. An agent reading
this file in order learns the same CAS → RBE sequence a human learns from the
sidebar.

Rung 1 (start with caching) → rung 2 (add remote execution) → rung 3 (configure
it) → rung 4 (task recipes). Operate, Understand and Contribute come after the
ladder; Reference is a lookup surface you can enter at any point.

This file is currently hand-maintained and will be generated from the navigation
and page frontmatter, so it cannot drift. The full corpus with page bodies is at
/llms-full.txt.

## Why NativeLink

- [Why NativeLink](https://docs.nativelink.com/use-cases): the problem, and a 30-second self-check for whether it's yours.

## Rung 1 — Start with caching

- [Start with caching](https://docs.nativelink.com/getting-started): the rung map — where you are and what's next.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.nativelink.com/getting-started/quickstart): install NativeLink and run your first cached build.
- [Connect your build tool](https://docs.nativelink.com/getting-started/connect-your-build): Bazel, Buck2, Siso, Pants, BuildStream, CMake via recc.
- [Chromium](https://docs.nativelink.com/getting-started/connect-your-build/chromium): building Chromium against NativeLink through Siso.
- [Shared cache](https://docs.nativelink.com/getting-started/shared-cache): move the cache off localhost so the team shares hits.

## Rung 2 — Add remote execution

- [Add remote execution](https://docs.nativelink.com/remote-execution): what execution adds on top of a working cache.
- [Local testing](https://docs.nativelink.com/rbe/local-testing): a scheduler and a worker on one machine.
- [Local Remote Execution](https://docs.nativelink.com/rbe/local-remote-execution): the toolchain mechanism that makes actions hermetic.
- [Examples](https://docs.nativelink.com/rbe/examples): runnable starting points.
- [Nix templates](https://docs.nativelink.com/rbe/nix-templates): Nix-based project templates.
- [Persistent workers](https://docs.nativelink.com/remote-execution/persistent-workers): pooled long-lived worker processes.

## Rung 3 — Configure it

- [Configuration](https://docs.nativelink.com/configuration/intro): the config model.
- [Basic configuration](https://docs.nativelink.com/configuration/basic): stores, servers, and services.
- [Compression](https://docs.nativelink.com/configuration/compression): shrink what you store and send.
- [Chunking](https://docs.nativelink.com/configuration/chunking): content-defined chunking and deduplication.

## Rung 4 — Task recipes

- [Task recipes](https://docs.nativelink.com/how-to): the task chooser.
- [OCI object storage](https://docs.nativelink.com/how-to/stores/oci-object-storage): an object-storage CAS backend.

## Operate in production

- [Operate](https://docs.nativelink.com/operate): what to watch, what to tune, what to do at 3am.
- [Production configuration](https://docs.nativelink.com/operate/production-config): the three-process production shape.
- [Tuning](https://docs.nativelink.com/operate/tuning): the lever table — signal, knob, direction, cost.
- [Deploy on Kubernetes](https://docs.nativelink.com/operate/deploy-kubernetes): the reference Kubernetes deployment.
- [Deploy on bare metal](https://docs.nativelink.com/operate/deploy-bare-metal): running on your own hardware.
- [Observability](https://docs.nativelink.com/operate/observability): the OTLP to Prometheus to Grafana pipeline.

## Understand it

- [Architecture](https://docs.nativelink.com/explanations/architecture): the four roles and how a request moves through them.
